top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a sharp, falsifiable prediction (Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and helical edge states from spin-orbit coupling and time-reversal symmetry alone) and its first experimental confirmation by Molenkamp's group in HgTe, with roughly two decades of transport, ARPES and materials work supporting the interpretation. It is mature and distinct from the 2016 topology prize, which concerned broken time-reversal Chern-type physics. The weakness is the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, which should be recorded openly and handled by a citation confined to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state. P002 has the cleaner two-name allocation and is a defensible second, but sits closer to the 2005 and 2012 metrology and atom-control prizes; P003 is promising but less mature, with experimental credit resting on one name.
